newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Sabena says considering more deals with Virgin.
newsitem.headline: Sabena says considering more deals with Virgin.

text.p: Belgian national carrier Sabena said on Thursday it might sign further cooperation deals on some of its key European routes with Richard Branson's Virgin Express low-cost regional airline.
Sabena, owned 49.5 percent by Swissair, signed a first commercial agreement with Brussels-based Virgin Express for flights between Brussels and London Heathrow in October.
"If the assessment for the London route is positive...we will examine three other possibilities...Rome, Barcelona and Paris," Sabena spokesman Eric Platteau told Reuters.

He said Sabena would wait until after the winter season to make a final assessment of its first cooperation deal with Virgin Express, launched in April after Branson bought 90 percent of Sabena rival EuroBelgian Airlines SA (EBA).
Platteau said no new deals should be expected before the second quarter of 1997.
Platteau said Sabena "categorically denied" a report in the weekly Trends/Tendances magazine saying Swissair was trying to persuade Virgin Express to buy most of Sabena's divisions.
Trends/Tendances said Swissair would only keep Sabena's regional subsidiary DAT, which it would then merge with its own Crossair subsidiary.
Virgin Express chief executive Jonathan Ornstein was not immediately available for comment.

Under the agreement on the London route, Virgin Express started operating Sabena's nine flights to Heathrow with Boeing 737-300 planes, allowing Sabena to use three Boeing 737s for longer-distance flights.
The cooperation with Virgin Express is seen by analysts as part of Sabena's drive to return to profit.

Sabena, which was recognized by Belgium's labour ministry as a company in difficulty, had a 1995 group loss before provisions of 530 million Belgian francs ($16.7 million) and a worse-than-expected two billion franc ($62.9 million) net loss in the first half of 1996.
Sabena chief executive Paul Reutlinger has pushed through a plan guaranteeing extra savings of 4.7 billion francs ($148 million), including two billion francs in labour-related cost reductions.
As part of the plan, Sabena has already sold its capacity cargo to Swissair's cargo division.
